newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY BCE GRAIN MKT STARTS SLOW, MINIMAL TURNOVER.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY BCE GRAIN MKT STARTS SLOW, MINIMAL TURNOVER.

text.p: The grains futures section of the Budapest Commodity Exchange started the year with a 19.4 million forints turnover compared with an average daily turnover of almost one billion forints last year.
"I only expect grains trade to pick up next Tuesday (on January 7)," said Ferenc Kiss of Agrokont.
He explained the slow start by the fact that most traders are still on holiday and those outside Budapest might have had difficulty reaching the capital due to heavy snowfalls.

The grains section will have its first Friday trade tomorrow, as from this year trade has been extended to all working days from the previous Tuesdays-to-Thursdays trading but Kiss said he only expects Monday and Friday trade to match the other three days by mid-1997.

"A lot of brokerages are based outside Budapest and it will take some client pressure for them to change habits," Kiss said. "The same happened a few years back when Wednesday trading was introduced".
Thursday's trade was made up of 24 milling wheat contracts, five feed wheat contracts and 13 feed barley contracts with milling wheat rising by limit for the August delivery.
Lot size is 20,000 kgs for all contracts.
